findings.text: the jets build expression is defined twice and the plan bounds both rather than unifying: `nova/equilibrium/fixed_points.py:204` (`_source_jets`) with its jitted `_row_program` at `:389`, and a second hand-written copy `scripts/prototypes/read_route/jets.py:229` (`_source_jets`) with its own `jax.jit(jax.vmap(_source_jets, in_axes=(0, None)))` at `:321`, which imports `packed_analytic_moments` from `nova.biot.polygonanalytic:2641` directly instead of reaching the production program — §3 states both are in scope and that bounding only the prototype does not meet the section, i.e. it pays the bounding work twice and leaves two programs to keep in step

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan introduces no new module; §2 bounds kernel terms by extending the existing per-helper private-tangent pattern (`nova/biot/completeelliptic.py:516`, `nova/biot/elliptic.py:1356`), and the mechanism it adds (a fixed-capacity scan or an exact tangent) hides the derivative graph behind the same primal interface rather than adding surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan requires bounding both definitions of one jets expression instead of consolidating on one owner (`nova/equilibrium/fixed_points.py`), and §1's census re-authors equation attribution already owned by `scripts/prototypes/order2/attribution.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2's tangents follow the repo's existing private-helper pattern (private scanned tangents, not exported), §1's deliverable is a research doc outside all four families, and §4 retires surface (the xfail marker and the fixture's expected-failure set) rather than adding any.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §1 proposes a compile census instrument and doc but cites only the cache-guard rows; it does not cite the machinery that already attributes expanded jaxpr equations to kernel call sites (`scripts/prototypes/order2/attribution.py`), already measures the read-route compile wall and executable bytes (`scripts/prototypes/read_route/measure.py`), already owns the lowered-jaxpr descent (`tests/jaxpr_scans.py`), or already holds the compile ledger (`docs/research/compile-cost-evidence.html`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no parallel thin layer is proposed: §2 reuses the two tangent forms the 2026-10-06 ruling already fixed and §4 retires the `KernelCompileBarrier` expected-failure set rather than wrapping it, so the honesty test is met by extension-and-retirement rather than by a new shell.
